Audit a finished figure for accessibility and honesty

Source: R/check_figure.R
check_figure.Rd

Checks a figure as it will be submitted, rather than the palette it was built from. palette_safety() can promise that the eight colours depictr ships stay apart under colour-vision deficiency, but it knows nothing about the figure in front of you: how many of those colours it uses, what you replaced them with, how small the text will be once the figure is squeezed into a journal column, or whether the only thing separating two groups is their colour. check_figure() reads the built plot and answers those questions with numbers.

Usage

check_figure(
  plot,
  width_cm = 17.78,
  render_width_cm = 17.78,
  min_delta_e = 5,
  min_text_pt = 6,
  metric = c("ciede2000", "cie76"),
  max_text_pt = NULL
)

Arguments

plot

A plot, as returned by any depictr plotting function, including one extended afterwards with +, or a multi-panel composite (see "Composites").

width_cm

The width, in centimetres, that the figure will occupy in the finished document. Defaults to 17.78 cm, the seven inches save_plot() draws at, which means no scaling.

render_width_cm

The width, in centimetres, that the figure is drawn at. Defaults to the same 17.78 cm. The ratio of the two widths is the factor every point size is multiplied by.

min_delta_e

The smallest acceptable colour difference, on the scale of metric, for the colour separability checks, and the smallest acceptable difference in lightness for the greyscale check. Defaults to 5, matching palette_safety().

min_text_pt

The smallest acceptable printed text size, in points, for the text around the panel and the text inside it alike. Defaults to 6, below the floor most journals set (see "Auditing at the printed size").

metric

The colour difference the colour separability checks measure: "ciede2000", the default, or "cie76", the Euclidean distance in CIELAB that earlier versions measured. "cie76" is kept so that earlier results can be reproduced, and a later release will remove it.

max_text_pt

The largest acceptable printed text size, in points, or NULL, the default, for no ceiling. When given, a text_size_max row is appended (see "What each check measures").

Value

A data frame with one row per check and columns check, measured, threshold, verdict ("pass", "fail" or "not applicable") and detail, a short note naming what produced the measurement. There are ten rows, and an eleventh, text_size_max, when max_text_pt is given. For a composite, the rows of each panel in turn, after a leading integer column panel.

Details

Every row carries the value it measured next to the threshold it was measured against, so a verdict can be argued with rather than merely accepted. A check passes when the measured value is at least the threshold. The one exception is text_size_max, a ceiling added when max_text_pt is given, which passes when the measured value is at most its threshold. A check that has nothing to measure, such as colour separability on a figure that encodes nothing by colour, reports NA and a verdict of "not applicable" instead of a free pass.

What each check measures

Colours and text are measured as drawn. A translucent colour is composited over the background it is drawn on with the alpha it is drawn with, so it is measured as the paler colour the reader sees. As ggplot2 draws them, bars, tiles, areas, densities, ribbons, polygons, violins, boxplots, crossbars and smooths apply a layer's alpha to their fill and leave the outline opaque. Lines, paths, segments, error bars and reference lines apply it to their colour, and points apply it to both. Any other geom is taken to apply it to both, the cautious assumption. A colour that carries its own alpha keeps it when the layer sets none, as ggplot2 draws it. A colour drawn at several alphas within one layer is measured at the smallest. Where marks overlap one another, the colour that shows depends on what lies beneath it, and that is not measured.

colour_separability is the smallest colour difference between two of the figure's encoding colours, by the CIEDE2000 formula (Sharma, Wu & Dalal, 2005) unless metric asks for the older CIE76. The three colour_separability_* rows repeat that measurement after simulating each dichromacy at full severity with simulate_cvd(). Encoding colours are the distinct colour and fill values that tell groups apart. A layer contributes its colours when it maps colour or fill to a discrete scale, even if it draws a single colour, or when it draws two or more. Groups drawn one per layer are therefore audited as they would be in one layer. A colour set as a constant, as in geom_point(colour = "red"), is left out, even when another layer sets a different one, and so is a lone colour passed through ggplot2::scale_colour_identity(). The audit cannot tell such a colour from decoration, so a colour meant to tell groups apart should be mapped, with ggplot2::scale_colour_manual() to fix its values. The outline colours, across every layer, are compared among themselves, and so are the fill colours, and the row reports the closest pair from either set. An outline is therefore never compared with its own fill, nor a group with itself as another layer draws it.

A continuous colour or fill scale, such as that of a heatmap, is a smooth ramp rather than a set of codes, and none of the colour rows audits it. When nothing else in the figure encodes by colour, each of them abstains with a detail that says so. Whether a ramp reads in order, to a reader with a colour-vision deficiency and in greyscale as well, depends on how evenly its lightness changes, which the audit does not measure. Prefer a perceptually ordered map, such as viridis or depictr's sequential and diverging ramps, over a rainbow (Crameri et al., 2020).

greyscale_separability is the smallest difference in CIE lightness between those same colours, which is what survives printing in black and white. It is the absolute difference in lightness, whichever metric the colour rows use.

text_size is the smallest point size of the text the theme draws around the panel: axis labels and titles, legends, facet strips, titles and captions. It is scaled by width_cm / render_width_cm, so a figure drawn seven inches wide and printed in an 8.9 cm column has every point size halved. Text drawn inside the panel is measured by annotation_text_size.

text_contrast is the WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio of the text that falls furthest short of its own threshold. Each text is measured against the background it is drawn on: a facet strip's fill for strip text, the legend box's fill for legend text, and the plot background for the rest. A translucent fill is measured as the colour it shows over what lies beneath it, and so is text drawn with an alpha. Text that is large at its printed size, 18 pt or 14 pt in bold, is held to 3:1, and other text to 4.5:1, as success criterion 1.4.3 asks. The row's threshold is the one that applies to the text it reports, and its detail names that text's colour, background, printed size and weight.

geometry_contrast is the smallest WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio of any encoded group's drawn colour against the panel background, or against the plot background where the panel paints none. Where a layer maps its outline colour to the same groups as its fill, each group counts the better of the two, since WCAG lets a border carry a graphical object's contrast. For a translucent colour, the detail names the colour, its alpha and the colour it is drawn as.

redundant_encoding counts how many of shape and line type also vary across the layers that draw the encoding colours. They are gathered as the colours are. A layer contributes the values it maps to a discrete scale, or the two or more it draws, and a shape or line type set as a constant is left out. Zero means the distinction between groups is carried by colour alone, which is the single most common way an otherwise careful figure becomes unreadable.

annotation_text_size is the smallest point size of the text drawn inside the panel, scaled as text_size is and held to the same min_text_pt. That text comes from layers such as ggplot2::geom_text() and ggplot2::geom_label(), from annotations, and from depictr's own cell values and labels. Its contrast is not measured, since it sits on the marks rather than on one background. A label that a layer builds only when the figure is drawn, as ggrepel builds its repelled labels, is not yet in the built plot, so it is not measured either.

text_size_max is reported only when max_text_pt is given, as the last row. It is the largest point size of all the text measured, around the panel and inside it, scaled as text_size is. It is the one row that passes at or below its threshold.

Limitations of the default palette

The eight-colour qualitative palette clears the colour-separability checks comfortably and fails greyscale_separability: its orange (#e69f00) and sky blue (#56b4e9) differ by only 0.79 in lightness, so they print as the same grey. The colourblind-safety guarantee depictr makes is about hue confusion, and it was never a claim about greyscale. A figure that may be printed in black and white should use fewer groups, or a sequential palette, or add a redundant shape or line type; the four leading colours of the palette are also not safe in greyscale, since the bluish green and the vermillion differ by 3.55. The threshold has been left where it is rather than moved to let the package's own defaults through.

The palette falls short on contrast as well. Four of its eight colours are below the 3:1 against white that WCAG asks of a graphical object: the orange at 2.25:1, the sky blue at 2.31:1, the grey at 2.85:1 and the yellow at 1.32:1. The orange is the second colour, so a default figure on white whose colour tells two or more groups apart fails geometry_contrast, and drawing its marks translucent lowers the ratio further. Opaque marks, the vermillion (#d55e00, at 3.87:1) in the orange's place and a redundant shape clear that row and redundant_encoding, as the first example below shows. The contrast-first order of depictr_palette() puts the vermillion second and the reddish purple third, and scale_colour_depictr() takes it as order = "contrast". Up to three groups then pass every colour row, and four keep 3:1 against white.

Auditing at the printed size

Text is drawn in points, so the size it prints at depends on the two widths. A figure drawn at the size it will be printed, as save_plot() draws one given width = 8.9, units = "cm", needs no scaling. Pass the saved width as both width_cm and render_width_cm, or leave both at their defaults. Given alone, width_cm audits the figure as though it had been drawn seven inches wide and then shrunk to fit. save_plot() with check = TRUE audits a figure at the width it saves it at, given as both.

The default min_text_pt of 6 is lenient. As their guidelines stood on 30 September 2026, PLOS asked for text of 8 to 12 pt and APA Style for 8 to 14 pt. Elsevier asked for 7 pt as a rule of thumb, and Nature for 5 to 7 pt, with panel labels at 8 pt. Pass the floor of the journal the figure is for as min_text_pt, and its ceiling, where it sets one, as max_text_pt. Nature's 7 pt applies to all text but the panel labels. The tags of a composite, where patchwork puts them, are not measured, but a panel label drawn as a panel's title or annotation is measured with the rest. The four pages are listed under References.

Composites

A composite, such as arrange_plots(), residual_diagnostics_plot() and model_report() return, is audited panel by panel. Each panel has its own scales, theme and text, so each is audited as it would be on its own. The reports are stacked under a leading integer column, panel, which only the report of a composite has. The widths are those of the whole composite. A panel's text keeps its point size whatever share of the width the panel takes, so the text of every panel scales by the same ratio.

Panels are numbered depth-first through any composite nested inside, in the order the composite holds them. That is the order patchwork tags them in, and the reading order of a grid filled row by row. A spacer or a guide area draws no figure of its own and takes no number. A wrapped element, such as a grob or a table, cannot be read, so it keeps its number and is left out of the report with a warning.

A panel's legend is measured with the panel, as the panel would draw it on its own, even when guides = "collect" gathers it into one legend for the composite. What the composite draws around its panels is not measured: the title, subtitle and caption of patchwork::plot_annotation() and the panel tags.

References

APA Style. Figures. https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/tables-figures/figures

Crameri F, Shephard GE, Heron PJ (2020). “The misuse of colour in science communication.” Nature Communications, 11(1), 5444. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7 .

Elsevier. Artwork sizing. https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/author/artwork-and-media-instructions/artwork-sizing

Machado GM, Oliveira MM, Fernandes LAF (2009). “A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency.” IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, 15(6), 1291–1298. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2009.113 .

Nature. Guide to preparing final artwork. https://www.nature.com/documents/nature-final-artwork.pdf

PLOS ONE. Figures. https://journals.plos.org/plosone/s/figures

Sharma G, Wu W, Dalal EN (2005). “The CIEDE2000 color-difference formula: Implementation notes, supplementary test data, and mathematical observations.” Color Research & Application, 30(1), 21–30. doi:10.1002/col.20070 .

World Wide Web Consortium (2023). “Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2.” W3C Recommendation, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/. Accessed 2026-08-18.

See also

palette_safety() for the palette in the abstract, and palette_preview() to look at it.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

# A figure that clears every check it can be held to: two well-separated
# colours, a redundant shape, and text left at the size it was drawn. It
# draws no text inside the panel, so that row is not applicable.
good <- ggplot(crop_yield, aes(rainfall, yield, colour = treatment,
                               shape = treatment)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#005b96", "#d55e00")) +
  theme_depictr()
check_figure(good)
#>                         check measured threshold        verdict
#> 1         colour_separability    50.12       5.0           pass
#> 2  colour_separability_protan    49.67       5.0           pass
#> 3  colour_separability_deutan    58.30       5.0           pass
#> 4  colour_separability_tritan    61.99       5.0           pass
#> 5      greyscale_separability    16.92       5.0           pass
#> 6                   text_size     8.80       6.0           pass
#> 7               text_contrast     8.45       4.5           pass
#> 8           geometry_contrast     3.87       3.0           pass
#> 9          redundant_encoding     1.00       1.0           pass
#> 10       annotation_text_size       NA       6.0 not applicable
#>                                                               detail
#> 1            Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 2            Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 3            Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 4            Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 5                 Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 in CIE lightness.
#> 6  Smallest text 8.80 pt, drawn at 17.78 cm and printed at 17.78 cm.
#> 7                Lowest-contrast text #4d4d4d on #ffffff at 8.80 pt.
#> 8                         Lowest-contrast colour #d55e00 on #ffffff.
#> 9                                         Colour is joined by shape.
#> 10                        The figure draws no text inside the panel.

# The same figure destined for an 8.9 cm journal column, where the text is
# half the size it looks on screen.
check_figure(good, width_cm = 8.9)
#>                         check measured threshold        verdict
#> 1         colour_separability    50.12       5.0           pass
#> 2  colour_separability_protan    49.67       5.0           pass
#> 3  colour_separability_deutan    58.30       5.0           pass
#> 4  colour_separability_tritan    61.99       5.0           pass
#> 5      greyscale_separability    16.92       5.0           pass
#> 6                   text_size     4.40       6.0           fail
#> 7               text_contrast     8.45       4.5           pass
#> 8           geometry_contrast     3.87       3.0           pass
#> 9          redundant_encoding     1.00       1.0           pass
#> 10       annotation_text_size       NA       6.0 not applicable
#>                                                              detail
#> 1           Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 2           Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 3           Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 4           Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 5                Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 in CIE lightness.
#> 6  Smallest text 8.80 pt, drawn at 17.78 cm and printed at 8.90 cm.
#> 7               Lowest-contrast text #4d4d4d on #ffffff at 4.40 pt.
#> 8                        Lowest-contrast colour #d55e00 on #ffffff.
#> 9                                        Colour is joined by shape.
#> 10                       The figure draws no text inside the panel.

# Saved at 8.9 cm in the first place, with save_plot(width = 8.9,
# units = "cm"), it is drawn at the size it prints, so both widths are 8.9.
check_figure(good, width_cm = 8.9, render_width_cm = 8.9)
#>                         check measured threshold        verdict
#> 1         colour_separability    50.12       5.0           pass
#> 2  colour_separability_protan    49.67       5.0           pass
#> 3  colour_separability_deutan    58.30       5.0           pass
#> 4  colour_separability_tritan    61.99       5.0           pass
#> 5      greyscale_separability    16.92       5.0           pass
#> 6                   text_size     8.80       6.0           pass
#> 7               text_contrast     8.45       4.5           pass
#> 8           geometry_contrast     3.87       3.0           pass
#> 9          redundant_encoding     1.00       1.0           pass
#> 10       annotation_text_size       NA       6.0 not applicable
#>                                                             detail
#> 1          Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 2          Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 3          Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 4          Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 of 2 encoding colours.
#> 5               Closest pair #005b96 and #d55e00 in CIE lightness.
#> 6  Smallest text 8.80 pt, drawn at 8.90 cm and printed at 8.90 cm.
#> 7              Lowest-contrast text #4d4d4d on #ffffff at 8.80 pt.
#> 8                       Lowest-contrast colour #d55e00 on #ffffff.
#> 9                                       Colour is joined by shape.
#> 10                      The figure draws no text inside the panel.

# Nature allowed no text above 7 pt but the panel labels. The axis titles
# here are 11 pt, so the ceiling row fails.
subset(check_figure(good, max_text_pt = 7), check == "text_size_max")
#>            check measured threshold verdict
#> 11 text_size_max       11         7    fail
#>                                                               detail
#> 11 Largest text 11.00 pt, drawn at 17.78 cm and printed at 17.78 cm.

# Each panel of a composite is audited, and a column says which panel each
# row describes. At base size 5, the second panel's text is too small.
small <- good + theme_depictr(base_size = 5)
both <- check_figure(arrange_plots(good, small))
both[both$verdict == "fail", c("panel", "check", "measured")]
#>    panel     check measured
#> 16     2 text_size        4
